At a glance

Arnold had 4,772 residents in the 2020 census and a median household income of $48,119. It became a borough in 1896 and a city in 1939. The map data holds 2,365 buildings, 2,444 address points and 120 listed places in the city.

Sources: Data USA, Wikipedia

Safety

Arnold police reported 39 violent crimes in the 9 months of 2024 they sent to the FBI, about 4.3 a month, up from about 2.2 a month in 2022 (22 in 10 months). Arnold sent no figures for 2023. The 2024 count works out to 8.4 per 1,000 residents, the city's highest rate since 2018 (9.7), and with three months missing the full-year number can only be higher. Police cleared 8 of the 39.

16 news-reported incidents in Arnold are on the police blotter, the earliest from 2022.

Serious crashes

PennDOT recorded 7 crashes in Arnold from 2005 through 2024 that seriously injured someone, 8 people in all. None killed anyone.

Neighborhoods and landmarks

A separate third-class city (borough 1896, city 1939) upriver from New Kensington, named for Major Andrew Arnold. It grew around the Chambers Glass Company (1891) and the 1913 Alcoa expansion. It shares the New Kensington-Arnold School District and the Advanced Manufacturing Park with New Kensington. 2020 population: 4,772.

Source: Wikipedia

Landmarks

New Kensington Production Works Historic District (Alcoa works). A 60-acre National Register district (May 7, 1998) with 35 industrial buildings from about 1899-1947. It includes Alcoa's original plant, which operated from 1891 to 1971, and is documented as HAER PA-337.

Along the Allegheny River, Seventh/Ninth Street to Sixteenth Street (New Kensington-Arnold) · Source: Wikipedia

New Kensington Advanced Manufacturing Park. The former Alcoa works and later Schreiber Industrial Park, straddling the New Kensington-Arnold line. It has been owned by a WCIDC-RIDC joint venture since 2023, and Re:Build Manufacturing operates there.

New Kensington / Arnold riverfront · Source: Westmoreland County

Chambers Window Glass Company site. Site of Arnold's 1891 window-glass works, one of the largest in the U.S. Innovations there included the Lubbers cylinder-drawing machine. It is documented by HAER.

North of Drey (Nineteenth) Street, west of Constitution Boulevard, Arnold · Source: Library of Congress

History

1852

Major Andrew Arnold settles the Arnold area.

The area around Arnold was first settled by Indian fighter Major Andrew Arnold, who gave the city its name. (Wikipedia also gives 1781 as a settlement date.)

Note: Sources differ: 1852 (settlement by Maj. Andrew Arnold) vs. 1781 (settled) in Wikipedia.

Source: City of Arnold

1867

Arnold Station opens.

Arnold Station, a railroad stop, was established on land given by the Arnold family.

Source: City of Arnold

1891

Chambers Glass Company opens in Arnold.

The Chambers Glass Company opened in Arnold and became one of the largest window-glass factories in the United States.

Source: Library of Congress

1896

Arnold becomes a borough.

Arnold was incorporated as a borough.

Source: Wikipedia

1913

Alcoa works expand into Arnold.

Alcoa's New Kensington Works expanded across the city line into Arnold.

Source: Wikipedia

1939

Arnold becomes a city.

Arnold was incorporated as a third-class city.

Source: Wikipedia

3 more from Arnold’s history

1965

New Kensington-Arnold School District formed.

The New Kensington-Arnold School District was formed on July 1, 1965. Also by 1965, Alcoa had opened its Alcoa Technical Center in Upper Burrell, having outgrown the Freeport Road lab.

Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)

2020

Population 12,170.

The 2020 census counted 12,170 New Kensington residents, 4,772 in Arnold and 11,758 in Lower Burrell.

Source: Wikipedia

2025

Re:Build begins production.

Re:Build finished upgrades to a 175,000-square-foot facility in the park, which straddles the New Kensington-Arnold line, and began manufacturing in early 2025.

Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)
